Synopsis:
Republican candidates are deploying anti-Muslim rhetoric as a campaign strategy ahead of the November 2026 midterms. Key figures include VP Vance attacking Senate candidate El-Sayed, Gov. Abbott targeting Muslim-led development in Texas, and Sen. Tuberville invoking "radical Islam" in Alabama. The trend coincides with growing Muslim political representation and comes as Republicans struggle with low Trump approval (~33%) and voter anxiety over cost of living, the U.S.-Iran war, and tariffs. Critics frame it as fear-mongering to deflect from substantive policy failures.
